diagnostic_evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.2 holds for the special case $\sigma_{\rm opt}$ and $z\in V_\beta$, where $r_N(x)$ also achieves the fastest rate  among all $\sigma>0$.

In Section \ref{sec:4}, we prove Theorem \ref{mainthm} and Theorem \ref{mainthm2} and their generalizations, including the optimality of the parameter $\sigma_{\rm opt}=\frac{\pi\sqrt{2(2-\beta)}}{\sqrt{\alpha}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims to prove that sigma_opt is the optimal clustering parameter, i.e. that it yields the fastest convergence among all sigma>0. Theorems mainthm/mainthm2 (and Section 4) establish only upper bounds O(e^{-sigma alpha sqrt N}) and O(e^{-eta^2 T}) for the constructed coefficients; no lower bound on the achievable error for sigma != sigma_opt is proved anywhere. Hence what is established is that sigma_opt maximizes the proven upper bound (and, for beta=0 only, attains Stahl's optimal rate), not that other sigma converge more slowly.

failure_location.quote: represents the optimal choice among all candidates in \eqref{eq:tapered2} for achieving the fastest convergence rate, and we therefore designate this value as $\sigma_{\rm opt}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the optimality claim as: sigma_opt maximizes the convergence rate guaranteed by Theorems mainthm/mainthm2, and for beta=0 this rate coincides with Stahl's best-approximation rate; drop claims that other sigma are provably slower unless lower bounds are supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'optimality of sigma_opt among all sigma' (intro, Section 4 description, Section 5 and conclusion) is unsupported for beta>0; only the maximization of the proven upper bound is justified.
issues.title: Optimality of sigma_opt among all sigma is asserted but only upper bounds are proved
issues.why_classification: The main upper-bound theorems survive untouched, but an advertised contribution (proved optimality of the clustering parameter) must be withdrawn or weakened for beta>0; proving it would require new lower-bound arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: from which we have $\big{|}Ce^{\frac{1}{\alpha}t}+z\big{|}\ge \frac{1}{2}Ce^{\frac{1}{\alpha}t}{\cal X}(\beta)$ for all $z\in \Omega_\rho$

issues.failure_explanation: For beta=0 the removed set is the full closed disk of radius 1 centred at -d, which contains [0,1-d] subset S_0, so S_0 is not contained in Omega_rho as defined, contradicting 'Omega_rho ⊃ S_beta'. Moreover the lower bound |Ce^{t/alpha}+z| >= (1/2)Ce^{t/alpha}X(beta) is only verified for two special families of points, and fails on Omega_rho as written (e.g. C=2, d=1/2, z=1.5e^{0.9 pi i} is in Omega_rho but |2+z|≈0.74<1 at t=0). The distance bound min|t-z|>=d used to get the factor 3/(2d) is also not valid (the distance from S_beta to the removed set is about d sin(beta pi/2)). These feed the bounds (eq:boundonr2) and (polynomial app).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Omega_rho as a genuine compact neighborhood of S_beta at positive distance from (-infinity,-C] (as in the figure), verify the lower bound |Ce^{t/alpha}+z|>=c Ce^{t/alpha} on it with some c>0 depending on beta, C, and adjust the constants in (eq:boundonr2), (polynomial app) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants in the r_2 bound and in E_PA are unjustified and the beta=0 case (the Stahl/Conjecture 1.1 case) has no valid neighborhood as written; the O(.) conclusions are not endangered once a proper neighborhood is chosen.
issues.title: Neighborhood Omega_rho is ill-constructed: excludes part of S_0 for beta=0 and claimed lower bounds fail on it
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition of the neighborhood and recomputation of constants repairs everything; rates and all theorem statements survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The interpolation nodes z_k (Fekete points) are placed on Gamma_rho, the very contour of the Hermite integral; then l_{n+1} vanishes on Gamma_rho, the integrand has poles on the path, and min_{t in Gamma_rho}|l_{n+1}(t)|=0, so the displayed estimate and (Runge12) are meaningless. The existence of rho>1 and n_0 independent of T (needed for uniformity, since r_2 depends on N_1) is asserted via citations rather than derived. Also (Runge12) bounds the C(Omega_rho)-norm although the estimate was set up on S_beta.

failure_location.quote: where $\Gamma_\rho$ is the boundary of $\Omega_\rho$, $s(\Gamma_\rho)$ is the length of $\Gamma_\rho$ satisfying $s(\Gamma_\rho)\le 2\pi(1+d)\le 3\pi$ and $\{z_k\}_{k=0}^n$ are the $n+1$ Fekete points on $\Gamma_\rho$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard Walsh/Hermite argument: interpolate at Fekete points of a compact K containing a neighborhood of S_beta, integrate over a level curve Gamma strictly outside K but inside C\(-infinity,-C] (fixed, independent of T), and bound max_Gamma|r_2| uniformly in T as in (eq:boundonr2); this yields the geometric rate with rho depending only on the geometry.
issues.overall_effect: The step establishing that the tail r_2 can be replaced by a polynomial of degree N_2=O(sqrt N_1) with error O(T^l e^{-T}) is not validly proved as written; this step underlies the low-degree polynomial claim in all main theorems.
issues.title: Hermite/Fekete argument for N_2=O(sqrt N_1) divides by min|l_{n+1}| over a contour containing the interpolation nodes (zero)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is a standard consequence of Walsh's theorem for functions analytic off a fixed slit; the repair is a routine rewrite of the interpolation estimate with no change to rates or statements.

issues.failure_explanation: By (ratappforzalphalog) the pole coefficient is sin(alpha pi)/((-1)^m alpha^2 pi) a_j^{(1)} + [sin(alpha pi)log C/((-1)^m alpha pi)+cos(alpha pi)/((-1)^m alpha)] a_j^{(0)}, where only a_j^{(1)} carries the factor (sqrt(jh)-T). The displayed formula multiplies all three terms by (sqrt(jh)-T), so the stated coefficients do not correspond to the constructed approximant. Both (eq:error1) and (eq:error1_2) also sum from j=0, where sqrt(jh)=0 appears in the denominator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by ã_j = (h p_j|p_j|^alpha/(2 sqrt(jh))) { sin(alpha pi)(sqrt(jh)-T)/(alpha^2 pi) + sin(alpha pi) log C/(alpha pi) + cos(alpha pi)/alpha } for 1<=j<=N_1, and start both sums at j=1.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicitly displayed coefficients are wrong; the theorems assert existence of coefficients and their proofs use the (correct) a_j^{(l)} from (eq:ECrat1C), so the rates are unaffected.
issues.title: Explicit LP coefficient formula for z^alpha log z misplaces the (sqrt(jh)-T) factor and uses j=0
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a displayed formula; no theorem, rate, or argument depends on the erroneous version.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem mainthmG defines sigma_opt = 2 sqrt(2-beta) pi/sqrt(alpha), which is sqrt2 times the value pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha) used in Theorems mainthm/mainthm2 on which its proof relies. With the stated value and beta=0, g≡1, the first branch of (eq: rateG1) at sigma=sigma_opt asserts an error O(e^{-2 sqrt2 pi sqrt(alpha N)}) for a degree-N rational approximant of x^alpha, contradicting Stahl's limit (eq:newmann1); the proof only supports the rates with the original sigma_opt, and the two branches are discontinuous at the stated threshold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the definition of sigma_opt in Theorem mainthmG by sigma_opt = pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha), consistent with Theorems mainthm and mainthm2.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Theorem mainthmG is false in the range pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha) < sigma <= 2 sqrt(2-beta) pi/sqrt(alpha); Theorem corner uses the correct sigma_k and is unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem mainthmG states sigma_opt with a wrong factor, yielding a rate that would beat Stahl's bound
issues.why_classification: A single forced constant correction restores the theorem to exactly what the proof establishes, with no loss of content.
